segments.text: The campus tutoring center matches student tutors to the courses they know best at the start of each term. A

fits their schedule. Courses that attract unusually heavy enrollment, such as introductory chemistry, receive additional tutoring hours so fewer learners face long waits. Tutors who cover more than one subject split their assigned hours between them equally. Midway through the term, staff examine these sign-up patterns and move unused hours toward whichever course shows the strongest demand.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處為句子主詞，緊接著的動作是「posts a printed grid」（張貼一份表格），指負責安排家教中心時段的人員，因此應填「coordinator」（協調員），呼應段落主旨——有人在管理媒合與排程作業。
動詞 posts 後面的受詞，並由「listing weekly time slots」修飾，說明這是一份列出時段的表格，故填「grid」（表格／方格圖），與前面的形容詞 printed（印製的）搭配合理。
此字修飾後面的「time slots」，說明表格上列出的是「每週」固定重複的時段，符合家教中心每學期開始就安排常態時段的情境，故填「weekly」。
「weekly time ___」加上後面「near the front desk」，指的是表格中列出的多個時間區段，且與後文單數的 slot 相呼應（學生各自選一個），故此處為複數「slots」。
此處為定冠詞，修飾後面的「front desk」，指的是文中已特定情境中那個櫃台（家教中心的服務台），為特指用法，故填「the」。
「near the front ___」為固定搭配，指公告張貼的位置在服務台附近，符合家教中心讓學生方便看到並報名的情境，故填「desk」。
此處為新分句的主詞，動作是「write their names beside…」，指的是查看表格並報名的人，也就是段落開頭提到的「student tutors」所服務的對象，故填「students」。
「students write ___ names」需要所有格代名詞，指學生自己的名字，故填「their」，與主詞 students（複數）一致。
「write their names ___ whichever slot」表示學生把名字寫在對應時段的「旁邊」以完成報名，符合表格簽名報名的情境，故填介系詞「beside」。
「whichever ___ fits their schedule」指學生從表格中選出一個符合自己課表的時段，與前面複數的 slots 呼應但此處為單數個別時段，故填「slot」。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: The campus tutoring center matches student tutors to the courses they know best at the start of each term. A coordinator posts a printed grid listing weekly time slots near the front desk, and students write their names beside whichever slot fits their schedule. Courses that attract unusually heavy enrollment, such as introductory chemistry, receive additional tutoring hours so fewer learners face long waits. Tutors who cover more than one subject split their assigned hours between them equally. Midway through the term, staff examine these sign-up patterns and move unused hours toward whichever course shows the strongest demand.

vocabulary that the program frequently misreads. Once corrections are complete, the finished transcript is posted publicly alongside the audio file before the show officially releases, giving listeners who prefer reading a dependable alternative to hearing it aloud.

gaps.explanationZh: it 是代名詞,回指前一句提到的 automatic transcription software(自動轉錄軟體),作為 Although 子句「it recognizes ordinary speech reasonably well」的主詞,指軟體本身辨識語音的能力。
ordinary 修飾 speech,指軟體能應付的「一般、普通」語音,與後半句列出的 unfamiliar names、technical terms、specific vocabulary(軟體常誤判的特殊內容)形成對比,凸顯讓步句 Although 的轉折。
reasonably 是副詞,修飾 well,表示軟體辨識一般語音的程度是「還算、相當」不錯,但非完美,呼應後文仍需人工編輯逐句檢查的必要性。
editor 是主詞,指「人類編輯」,與前句的自動軟體(automatic transcription software)形成對比,說明即使軟體辨識尚可,仍需要人工角色來把關逐字稿品質。
examines 是及物動詞,主詞為 a human editor,採現在式第三人稱單數形態(examines),與 still 搭配表示編輯「仍會」仔細檢查逐字稿初稿。
draft 指軟體產出、尚待校正的逐字稿初稿,呼應前句 a rough written record,說明編輯所檢查的對象正是這份未經修正的草稿。
checking 是現在分詞,引導說明編輯「examines」時具體在做什麼動作,後接受詞 unfamiliar names, technical terms, and specific vocabulary,構成分詞片語補充描述檢查內容。
names 與後方的 technical terms、specific vocabulary 並列,指軟體常誤判的「人名等專有名詞」,屬於編輯需要特別檢查、軟體容易辨識錯誤的內容之一。
terms 與 technical 搭配構成 technical terms(專業術語),是編輯需檢查、軟體常誤讀的另一類內容,與 names、specific vocabulary 並列成三項清單。
specific 修飾 vocabulary,指「特定、專門」的詞彙,涵蓋前面 names、terms 之外其他容易被軟體誤讀的用字,呼應句末 the program frequently misreads 的說明。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Podcast production teams increasingly rely on automatic transcription software to generate a rough written record of every recorded episode. Although it recognizes ordinary speech reasonably well, a human editor still examines each draft closely, checking unfamiliar names, technical terms, and specific vocabulary that the program frequently misreads. Once corrections are complete, the finished transcript is posted publicly alongside the audio file before the show officially releases, giving listeners who prefer reading a dependable alternative to hearing it aloud.

Subject: Your Recent Air Quality Test Results

Dear Ms. Alvarez,

Thank you for letting our team collect an air sample from your backyard on March 14. The results are ready.

Particulate levels at your property were within the normal residential range. Carbon monoxide readings were slightly higher than the neighborhood average, though still below any level of concern. We recommend keeping windows open while cooking to help lower this further.

We would like to schedule a follow-up test around June 14 to confirm the readings stay stable. Please reply with a date that works for you.

Thank you for taking part in our neighborhood monitoring project.

Sincerely,
Priya Nandan
Riverside Environmental Lab

questions.stem: Where was the air sample collected?

options.text: From the resident's backyard
From inside the resident's kitchen
From the neighborhood park
From a nearby street corner

academic.title: How Neighborhood Associations Shape Local Decisions
academic.text:
In many cities, small groups of volunteer residents organize themselves into neighborhood associations to represent local interests to city government. These associations typically form when residents notice a shared concern, such as traffic safety, a proposed construction project, or the loss of a public park. Once established, an association often collects signatures for a petition, which members present at a city council meeting or mail directly to elected officials. Petitions alone rarely change policy, but they signal that a measurable number of residents care about an issue, which can prompt officials to investigate further.

Neighborhood associations also hold regular public meetings where residents raise concerns directly, ask questions of visiting officials, and vote on positions the association will formally support. These meetings give quieter voices a structured setting to speak, something an individual phone call to city hall rarely achieves. Over time, a consistently active association can gain enough credibility that planning departments consult it before finalizing decisions, such as where to place a new crosswalk or how to zone an empty lot. This influence remains informal in most cities; associations hold no legal veto over municipal decisions. Even so, officials who ignore a well-organized association's repeated objections risk facing public criticism at the next election, which gives neighborhood groups real, if indirect, leverage over local policy.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.text: Neighborhood associations give residents informal but real influence over city decisions
Neighborhood associations possess full legal veto power over any municipal project they dislike, allowing them to block construction outright
City law requires residents to form a registered association before any local construction can proceed
Neighborhood associations exist primarily to plan social gatherings and events for local residents

questions.explanationZh: 文章主旨:社區協會透過請願與公開會議,對地方決策產生非正式但實際的影響力。文章明確指出協會沒有法定否決權,故b錯;文中未提及強制註冊規定,故c錯;協會目的並非辦理社交活動,故d錯。

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "leverage" most nearly mean?

options.text: A sum of money paid informally to influence officials' decisions
A legally protected right or entitlement guaranteed by statute
A formal vote officially cast during a scheduled election
The power to influence a result

questions.explanationZh: 此處leverage意指「影響局勢的力量」,呼應協會能促使官員正視其意見。文章明確說協會沒有法定否決權,故「受法律保障的權利」錯;文中未提及金錢給付,故「私下付錢影響官員」錯;也未提正式投票,故「選舉中的正式投票」錯。

questions.stem: Based on the passage, what can be inferred about an individual resident who calls city hall alone?

options.text: Alone, their concern carries less influence than one raised through an association
Their phone call is automatically added to whichever petition the association next circulates
City hall keeps absolutely no written or electronic record of individual residents' phone calls
City officials must legally respond to every individual phone call within a specific, legally mandated number of business days

questions.explanationZh: 文章指出個人打電話「rarely achieves」與有組織會議相同的效果,可推論個人意見較難單獨產生影響力,故「個人單獨提出的意見,影響力不如透過協會提出」為合理推論。文章未提法定回覆期限、電話自動併入請願或市府不留紀錄,均缺乏文本依據。

questions.stem: How does the second paragraph relate to the first?

options.text: It shifts to a completely different topic, focusing on how associations organize social gatherings
It describes an additional method, public meetings, that associations use alongside petitions to influence officials
It summarizes the same information from the first paragraph using different wording
It contradicts the first paragraph by showing that petitions never influence local government

questions.explanationZh: 第二段介紹協會另一種發揮影響力的方式——公開會議,是第一段請願方式之外的補充,而非否定第一段內容、轉向社交活動,或只是換句話重述第一段。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention that neighborhood associations "hold no legal veto over municipal decisions"?

options.text: To explain why most residents choose not to join an association
To argue that neighborhood associations should be granted more formal legal authority
To criticize city governments for ignoring resident concerns entirely
To clarify that their influence, while real, is informal rather than an enforceable legal power

questions.explanationZh: 作者提到協會「沒有法定否決權」,是為了釐清協會的影響力屬於非正式性質,而非具有強制力的法律權力。文章並非主張應給予協會更多法定權力,也沒有解釋居民為何不加入協會,更沒有全盤批評政府忽視居民意見。

segments.text: A community center in one neighborhood now lets residents borrow tools instead of buying their own equipment. Each

item receives a careful inspection so it stays safe for whoever needs it next. Anyone joining for the first time skips the standard enrollment fee completely. That small incentive persuades more households to give the program a try.

gaps.explanationZh: 此句主詞指借用工具的居民個人,「Each participant」意為「每位參與者」,呼應前句 residents borrow tools 的身分,且與後面 may keep 的單數動詞一致,故填 participant。
情態動詞 may 之後須接原形動詞,語意為「可以保留」一項工具兩週,故填 keep。
與後方並列的 saw、ladder(鋸子、梯子)同屬可借用的工具項目,此處指「水平儀」,故填 level。
用於連接列舉清單中的最後一個選項(saw, or ladder),表示三者擇一借用,故填 or。
介系詞 for 後接時間長度 two weeks,表示保留工具的期限,故填 for。
two 為數量詞,後面須接複數名詞表示「兩週」,對應歸還前可保留工具的期限,故填 weeks。
介系詞 before 之後須接動名詞形式,表示歸還前所做的動作「攜帶」,故填 bringing。
介系詞 to 表示動作的對象或方向,指把工具交還給志工,故填 to。
承接下句 Every returned item receives a careful inspection 可知,負責檢查歸還工具的人即是志工,故此處填 volunteer。
此處為過去分詞作形容詞,修飾 item,表示「已歸還的」物品才會接受仔細檢查,故填 returned。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: A community center in one neighborhood now lets residents borrow tools instead of buying their own equipment. Each participant may keep a level, saw, or ladder for two weeks before bringing it to a volunteer. Every returned item receives a careful inspection so it stays safe for whoever needs it next. Anyone joining for the first time skips the standard enrollment fee completely. That small incentive persuades more households to give the program a try.

dailyLife.text:
Historic Town Hall Restoration Nears Completion

Riverdale — Workers are finishing a two-year restoration of the town hall using a $400,000 heritage grant. The project repaired the roof and replaced damaged wooden beams while keeping the original brick walls and stone entrance steps intact. Restoration crews matched new materials as closely as possible to the building's original 1920s design. City officials say the building will reopen to the public on October 3, with a small ceremony planned that morning. The town hall has served as a meeting space and event venue since it was first built.

options.text: Ticket sales from public events
A local property tax increase
A donation from a private company
A $400,000 heritage grant

options.text: They tried to preserve the building's original historical appearance
They replaced all original materials with modern, low-cost alternatives

questions.explanationZh: 文章提到修復團隊盡量讓新材料貼近1920年代原始設計,並保留原有磚牆與石階,可推論其目標是維持建築原有的歷史外觀,而非改用低成本現代材料、放著屋頂樑柱不修,或把建築改造成完全不同的樣貌。

academic.title: The Revival of a Regional Ceramic Craft
academic.text:
For much of the twentieth century, a traditional style of ceramic glazing in one rural region nearly disappeared. Fewer young people wanted to learn the slow, difficult steps needed to mix and apply the glaze correctly, and most trained potters had grown old or stopped working. By the 1990s, only a handful of elderly craftspeople still remembered the full process.

A local arts festival changed this trend. Organizers invited the remaining potters to demonstrate their techniques in public, live, in front of curious visitors. The demonstrations drew unexpected crowds, and several younger attendees asked whether they could learn the craft themselves. Festival organizers responded by setting up a small apprenticeship program, pairing each interested learner with an experienced potter for hands-on training.

Over the next decade, the program trained dozens of new potters. Apprentices spent months practicing basic shaping before they were allowed to attempt the traditional glaze at all, since a mistake at that late stage could ruin weeks of earlier work. Today, the craft is taught regularly at the festival, and pieces made in the traditional style are sold at markets across the region. Older potters who once feared the tradition would vanish now describe the current interest as the strongest it has been in decades, crediting the festival for giving the craft a public stage it had long lacked.

questions.stem: What eventually happened after the festival began featuring live demonstrations by the remaining potters?

options.text: The remaining potters refused to teach anyone the craft
The craft was banned from being sold at markets
The festival stopped inviting potters after the first year
An apprenticeship program was created to train new potters

questions.explanationZh: 文章提到藝術節邀請僅存的陶藝師公開示範後,吸引年輕人詢問學習機會,於是主辦單位設立學徒制度加以培訓。文章明確指出這項工藝如今仍在藝術節定期教授、作品也在市集販售,並非停辦活動或陶藝師拒絕傳授技藝。

questions.stem: In the passage, what does "vanish" most nearly mean?

options.text: Change into a new form
Spread to other regions

segments.text: Overnight train operators calculate sleeper cabin prices using a formula that accounts for how far the train travels, seasonal demand, and how far in advance a passenger books. During

of travelers seeking a place to sleep on board. Routes spanning greater distances typically cost more than short regional connections. Passengers who reserve several weeks early often receive a meaningful discount.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處與後面的 travel periods 搭配成 peak travel periods（旺季/尖峰旅遊期間），呼應下文 major holidays 導致票源稀少、票價上漲的情境，故填 peak。
peak travel periods 為固定搭配，periods 指「一段期間」，指涉旅遊需求特別高的時段，與後文 such as major holidays 舉例呼應，故填 periods。
such as 為固定片語，用來引出前述 peak travel periods 的具體例子，即後面的 major holidays，故填 as。
此處緊接 such as major，需要一個名詞說明是哪種尖峰期間，holidays（假期）正是造成旅遊需求暴增、票價上漲的典型例子，故填 holidays。
主詞 rates 之後需要動詞說明票價的變化，climb sharply（急遽攀升）符合旺季票源稀少、需求大於供給時價格上漲的邏輯，故填 climb。
此處連接「rates climb sharply」與其原因子句「available berths become scarce...」，because 表示因果關係，說明票價上漲是因為臥鋪稀少，故填 because。
此處主詞需為可預訂的臥鋪空間，全句主題是 sleeper cabin（臥鋪車廂），berths 指火車上的臥鋪／床位，與 become scarce（變得稀少）及後文 a place to sleep on board 呼應，故填 berths。
berths become 之後需要形容詞說明臥鋪的供給狀況，scarce（稀少的）符合旺季時床位供不應求、進而推高票價的邏輯，故填 scarce。
relative to 為固定片語，意為「相對於」，用來比較臥鋪數量與尋求床位的旅客人數，故填 to。
此處指「旅客的人數」，number of travelers 說明相對於稀少臥鋪的是大量尋求床位的旅客人數，符合供需失衡導致漲價的語意，故填 number。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Overnight train operators calculate sleeper cabin prices using a formula that accounts for how far the train travels, seasonal demand, and how far in advance a passenger books. During peak travel periods, such as major holidays, rates climb sharply because available berths become scarce relative to the number of travelers seeking a place to sleep on board. Routes spanning greater distances typically cost more than short regional connections. Passengers who reserve several weeks early often receive a meaningful discount.

academic.title: The Physics of Sound Inside a Noise-Cancelling Device
academic.text:
Active noise-cancelling headphones rely on a principle of wave physics called destructive interference to reduce the ambient sound a listener perceives. A small microphone mounted on the device continuously captures the surrounding sound wave, particularly low-frequency, repetitive noise such as an airplane engine's hum or a running fan. This signal is fed to a processor that generates a second wave with the same amplitude and frequency as the captured noise but shifted precisely out of phase, meaning its peaks align with the original wave's troughs and vice versa.

When the device emits this inverted wave through the same speaker that plays music or podcast audio, the two waves arrive at the listener's ear at nearly the same instant and interfere with one another. Where the peak of one wave coincides with the trough of the other, the combined air pressure change is close to zero, and the listener perceives comparatively little of the original noise. This process works best against steady, predictable, low-frequency sounds, since the processor can track and invert them with minimal delay. Sudden, irregular sounds, such as a dog barking or a door slamming, change too quickly for the system to generate an accurate inverted wave in time, which is why noise-cancelling devices are far less effective against sharp or unpredictable noise than against a steady mechanical drone.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.text: Active noise-cancelling headphones use destructive interference to reduce steady ambient noise.

Active noise-cancelling headphones are equally effective at silencing every kind of sound a listener might encounter, from steady mechanical drones to sudden, unpredictable noises such as a barking dog or a slamming door.
Active noise-cancelling headphones raise the volume of music until it overpowers any background noise.
Active noise-cancelling headphones physically block sound waves from reaching the ear by sealing the ear canal with a solid barrier built into the ear cup.

questions.explanationZh: 文章主旨在說明主動降噪耳機透過產生與環境噪音相位相反的聲波,利用波的干涉原理抵銷穩定的環境噪音。文章明確指出此技術對突發、不規則聲音效果較差,並非對所有聲音都同樣有效;耳機也不是靠實體屏障封住耳道阻隔聲音,更不是把音樂音量調高蓋過噪音。

questions.explanationZh: 文章最後提到系統處理突發、不規則聲音時來不及即時產生準確的反向聲波,故關門聲這類快速聲音較難被抵銷。文章沒有提到麥克風有音量偵測上限、關門聲不會產生可偵測的聲波,也沒有說喇叭功率不足以播放大聲聲音。
